prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No open or discoverable solution provides safe smartphone care in 7,000 languages; deployed health assistants cover a handful. WHO's S.A.R.A.H. launched in 8 languages and is now a research prototype not in public deployment (https://www.who.int/news/item/02-04-2024-who-unveils-a-digital-health-promoter-harnessing-generative-ai-for-public-health); Ada's symptom checker lists 7 languages (https://www.mobihealthnews.com/news/ada-health-launches-swahili-language-version-its-app). The strongest open building block is Meta's Omnilingual ASR, Apache 2.0, covering about 1,600 languages but with character error rate under 10% for only 78% of them and much weaker for low-resource languages (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.09690); speech recognition is not clinical care. Medical LLM accuracy drops sharply in African languages, by about 38.6 points for open-weight models on a 13-language clinical benchmark (https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/177288). Honest limit: open multilingual speech and translation models are real prior art, so tasks must target the clinical-safety and validation gap in low-resource languages, not re-release translation.
